key_insight: Convert temporally-consistent deformable Gaussian scaffolds into free-form bones plus a refined mean-curvature skeleton to produce intuitive, controllable rigs that preserve complex non‑rigid surface deformations.
problem_solved: Automatic creation of animatable, kinematically-structured rigs from category-level deformable reconstructions — bridging the gap between expressive surface representations (deformable Gaussians) and practical, controllable skeleton-based animation.
method: Compress temporally-consistent deformable Gaussians into free-form 'skelebones' that approximate non-rigid surface deformation while remaining locally coherent.
Extract a Mean Curvature Skeleton from canonical Gaussians and temporally refine it to produce a stable kinematic backbone.
Assemble a Scaffold–Skin rig by binding the surface (skin) to the skelebones and expose per-bone 'level-of-dynamics' controls for varying animation complexity and fidelity.
impact: Enables scalable, category-level automatic rigging that keeps rich non-rigid detail while providing intuitive kinematic control — useful for faster animation pipelines, data generation, and downstream learning-based motion tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Gaussian scaffold → free-form bones → mean-curvature skeleton → skinned output (sequence arrows).
Side-by-side comparisons: raw deformable Gaussians vs compressed skelebones vs final skinned mesh in motion.
Overlay visualization: skeleton and bone weights drawn over the Gaussian scaffold (color-coded influence).
Control UI mockup: per-bone 'level-of-dynamics' sliders and resulting deformation differences (before/after frames).
paper_title: GaussiAnimate: Reconstruct and Rig Animatable Categories with Level of Dynamics
paper_authors: Jiaxin Wang, Dongxin Lyu, Zeyu Cai, Zhiyang Dou, Cheng Lin
